title: Frequency of postprocedural masticatory muscle pain following arthroscopy and arthrocentesis for structural temporomandibular joint disorders
summary:
Temporomandibular joint disorders, such as joint degeneration, inflammation, or displacement of the joint disc, can cause pain and difficulties opening the mouth and chewing. For selected conditions, the joint is flushed and may also be examined and treated using a small camera. Pain in the chewing muscles may occur after these procedures. This study investigates how often this happens, when the symptoms begin, and how severe they are.

At University Medical Center Mainz, 23 adult patients will be assessed before surgery and followed for six months afterward. Before surgery, patients have no or only mild chewing muscle symptoms that do not require treatment. Examinations take place before surgery and after two weeks, two months, four months, and six months. Patients also complete questionnaires before surgery and after two and six months. These assessments investigate possible associations between muscle pain, jaw function, psychological well-being, and quality of life. Treatment is provided as part of usual medical care independently of study participation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥18 years, capacity to provide informed consent, and written informed consent to study participation.
Structural temporomandibular joint disorder requiring treatment: symptomatic disc displacement with or without reduction, temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis including adapted degenerative joint disease or progressive osteoarthritis, or temporomandibular joint arthritis.
Clinical indication for and consent to unilateral or bilateral arthrocentesis or arthroscopy with arthrocentesis.
No or only minimal masticatory muscle symptoms at the initial examination that do not require treatment.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Inability to provide informed consent or absence of consent to study participation.
2. Age <18 years.
3. Acute temporomandibular joint trauma during the study period.
4. Temporomandibular joint infection immediately before or during data collection.
5. Chronic pain syndrome.
6. Botulinum toxin treatment of the masticatory muscles within six months before enrollment.
7. Conditions or previous treatments precluding surgery, particularly medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, untreated tumors of the jaw or scalp, previous radiotherapy to the head and neck region, chemotherapy within the preceding ten years, or severe systemic disease precluding general anesthesia (ASA >III).
8. Conditions interfering with pain assessment or influencing pain perception, particularly psychiatric disorders, especially those associated with antidepressant use.
Protocol-defined criteria for early discontinuation include withdrawal of consent, trauma to the temporomandibular joint region, bleeding requiring repeat surgery, relevant wound infection, substantial wound-healing impairment with prolonged recovery, facial muscle dysfunction due to facial nerve injury persisting for more than two weeks, hearing loss or hearing impairment, and complete absence of symptomatic improvement after surgery. Additional discontinuation criteria include botulinum toxin treatment of the masticatory muscles during study participation or the new occurrence of a condition or treatment defined as an exclusion criterion.
